disclaimer: Figures are “up to” amounts from SpaceX’s Form 424(b)(4). A release makes shares eligible to be sold under the lock-up; it is not a forecast that holders will sell. Goldman Sachs, as underwriters’ representative, may release shares earlier. Company trading windows, Rule 144, affiliate volume limits, and unvested awards can still block a sale. Approximate value uses the price shown at the top of this page and will move with it.

freeFloatNote: SpaceX does not publish an official free-float figure. 4.33 billion (31.9% of shares outstanding) is FloatCap’s estimate of circulating supply minus unrestricted insider holdings, as of its 10-Q / 424(b)(4) review. Percentages of free float below use this denominator and are estimates.

priceTrigger.condition: Additional Release Shares (up to 455.8 million, 10% of the 180-day group, excluding Rule 144 affiliates) would have been released on the First Earnings Release Date only if the Nasdaq closing price was at least 30% above the $135.00 IPO price — $175.50 — on at least five of the ten consecutive trading days ending on, and including, that date.
priceTrigger.firstEarningsReleaseDate: The prospectus defines the First Earnings Release Date as the second full Nasdaq trading day immediately after the public release of quarterly results for the quarter ended 30 Jun 2026. Q2 results were filed on 4 Aug 2026; the second full trading day after that was 6 Aug 2026 (assuming an after-close release on 4 Aug; the 8-K does not state the time of day).
priceTrigger.outcomeNote: SpaceX has not filed a statement confirming whether the $175.50 test was met. Yahoo Finance daily closes (regular session) in every 10-trading-day window ending on 4 Aug or 6 Aug 2026 ranged from $108.27 to $125.33 — all well below $175.50. This page therefore uses the prospectus’s 797.6 million December 8 remainder, which applies if the Additional Release Shares were not released. The alternative if they had been released is 328.4 million.

holders.who: Pre-IPO holders whose shares are on the standard 180-day schedule (employees, early investors, and other holders not in the extended group or Musk’s 366-day category). The prospectus describes “a variety of other terms” for 180 days, with timed automatic releases.

“Certain shareholders” agreed to remain locked until the release of results for the quarter ending 30 Jun 2027, with staged automatic releases. The prospectus names Gwynne Shotwell, President and COO, as having agreed to put the vast majority of her shares in this extended period. Later compilations also place CFO Bret W. Johnsen in the group. The filing does not publish a complete holder list.
holders.source: 424(b)(4); FloatCap derivation of the release table

holders.who: All of the shares of common stock owned by him. No early-release provisions. Class B shares (10 votes) are unlisted and must convert 1:1 into Class A before they can trade. Separate unvested performance awards remain subject to their own vesting milestones after the lock-up ends.

Unregistered shares issued in the Cursor (Anysphere) and Mesh Optical deals. These are not part of the IPO lock-up table. Public resale is first limited by Rule 144’s holding period; a separate contractual lock-up may still apply (Cursor terms are not fully public).

unvestedBreakdown.name: SpaceX CEO Award
unvestedBreakdown.note: 15 tranches; each requires a market-cap milestone from $500B to $7.5T and a permanent human colony on Mars of at least one million inhabitants, plus continued employment.

unvestedBreakdown.name: AI CEO Award
unvestedBreakdown.note: 12 tranches; market-cap milestones from $1.065T to $6.565T and off-Earth data centers delivering 100 terawatts of compute per year, plus continued employment. As of 31 Mar 2026 the company treated both performance awards as improbable for accounting.
